prize_parts.citation: for the design and formulation of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable systemic delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I keep B019 as my preferred single prize part. The scientific argument is unchanged and I think it has been strengthened by Aili's independent statement of it: pH-dependent charge, packing and non-bilayer phase behaviour, and controlled mixing together explain both encapsulation and endosomal release, and this can be stated as a general physical-chemical principle and tested quantitatively with pKa tuning and phase diagrams. The record is the most complete on the shortlist on the criterion the chair and several colleagues stress, namely maturity: decades of independent work, approved siRNA drugs, and mRNA vaccines at pandemic scale. The delivery chemistry is the part of the mRNA story that the 2023 Medicine prize did not recognise. On attribution I stay with the Vancouver line. The ionizable-lipid concept, nucleic-acid encapsulation at low pH with charge neutrality at physiological pH, and the formulation methods that gave reproducible particles come from Cullis, Madden and Hope, and each name maps to an identifiable step, which keeps the three-person cut defensible.
statement.case_against: The objections remain real and I do not think round 1 removed them. B019 may be judged pharmaceutical formulation more than a discovery of a chemical principle, and the 2023 Medicine prize may make the area feel already honoured. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan have credible claims that a three-name limit forces me to exclude. B019 also has only two explicit supporters against four for B056, and I should not pretend that I can win the argument by counting. I also have to admit that my own field leans me toward the phase-behaviour explanation and that I may undervalue the empirical screening line.

responses.point: Linke asked whether Cullis, Madden and Hope is defensible without Anderson and Langer, since that cut decides whether the candidate is viable, and posed the chair question of whether the decisive step was Vancouver encapsulation or lipidoid screening.
responses.response: My answer is yes, with a stated rule: credit the people who established the concept and the working formulation chemistry. Ionizable amino lipids that are neutral in blood and charged in the endosome, encapsulation at acidic pH, and reproducible particle formation were in place in Vancouver before the lipidoid libraries. Anderson and Langer made a powerful optimisation and discovery route, and I regard that as a genuine contribution, but a route to better lipids within an established design principle is not the same as establishing the principle. I accept that a reasonable member can see it the other way, and that is why I list the Anderson question openly as my main uncertainty. I also thank Linke for the careful point on B026, and I agree that condensates are not yet mature enough for 2026.

responses.point: Aili supports B019 with Cullis, Madden and Anderson, and holds that the lipid screening line produced the potent lipids used in the approved siRNA product and later mRNA work.
responses.response: We agree on the science and on the complementarity with the 2023 prize, and I value that a second soft-matter colleague reaches the same physical-chemical reading independently. We differ only on the third name. I do not see evidence that the lipidoid line was part of the founding discovery rather than a later parallel optimisation, and several of the lipids in the approved products came from the pKa-optimised ionizable-lipid design line. I would not oppose a Cullis, Madden, Anderson trio if the committee decides that screening was decisive, and I would rather we reach a five-vote B019 trio than split on the third name. If the exchange comes down to Hope versus Anderson alone, I would want the priority record checked before we vote.

responses.point: Chabes prefers B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, but ranks B019 as his fallback, and notes that PROTAC and cereblon are two lines held in one citation.
responses.response: This is the exchange that matters most for a majority. Chabes's own reservation, that pairing the engineered PROTAC concept with Handa's mechanism result is a judgement call, is the same kind of attribution difficulty I carry for B019, so neither of us has a clean credit case. The difference I would press is maturity: B019 has finished clinical and societal validation, while the PROTAC arm of B056 has none. I would ask Chabes whether the lack of an approved degrader is enough to move him to his B019 fallback this year, or whether he regards it as a matter of waiting a few years. I do not move to B056 on the strength of support counts.

responses.point: Aqvist moved to B056 after the opening ballots on the grounds of breadth of support and defensibility to the Academy, and keeps B058 and B016 as alternatives.
responses.response: I accept that breadth of support matters when a prize must be defended, but I treat it as evidence of cross-field interest and not as a substitute for judging the scientific case. On the substance, Aqvist himself names the key weakness: the approved imid drugs were found empirically, and the mechanism was resolved afterwards, so B056 would reward a concept and a mechanism more than a completed modality. B019 is the reverse. The design principle is established and the products are in patients. I would be glad to see Aqvist state what evidence on clinical maturity would settle this for him.

responses.point: Zou moved from perovskites to B056 on mechanism, attribution and breadth, citing ternary-complex structures, but says waiting may be wiser if the clinical proof is judged insufficient.
responses.response: Zou's point about ternary-complex structure is the strongest physical argument for B056 and I take it seriously: cooperativity in a three-body equilibrium is real physical chemistry. But Zou also concedes that the committee may prefer to wait, and that Ciulli is left out of the trio. For a first-year member this is a decisive reason for caution. A prize whose trio is described by its supporters as leaving out a figure who made the field rational is more exposed than one with a clear step-by-step Vancouver line.

uncertainties: Whether the decisive credit lies with the Vancouver line (Cullis, Madden, Hope) or should include the lipidoid screening line (Anderson, Langer), and where MacLachlan belongs; I have not verified patent and priority details.
Whether a majority sees ionizable lipid nanoparticles as chemistry in its own right or as pharmaceutical formulation, and whether the 2023 Medicine prize weighs against it.

Whether B056 will be judged mature enough in 2026 without an approved PROTAC drug, and whether the committee would treat the lack of a five-vote position as a reason to prefer the more mature candidate.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B019. I work on lipid self-assembly and membranes, so I am close to the subject matter scientifically and may overweight the phase-behaviour explanation. I am a Lund University colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and my research overlaps with Daniel Aili on self-assembly and with Peter Brzezinski on membranes. I have no personal or institutional connection to any credited candidate and see no need for recusal.
